results.attack: Cloud creates a content object for the homelab key without any device secret
results.detail: age -d exit 0; plaintext=b'object made by the cloud, which holds on'. Encryption to the homelab key proves nothing about origin; ingest must bind every object to a device-signed record (header MAC) before it counts.

results.attack: Worker substitutes the homelab recipient; device has no pin
results.detail: Device encrypted to the key the Worker supplied; the cloud decrypted with its own identity. Every upload after enrollment is readable by the cloud.

results.attack: Same substitution; device checks SHA-256(bundle) against the kit pin
Dedup secret delivered in plaintext through the Worker; cloud tests a known file
results.detail: Breaks ADR-0001's 'the cloud cannot test for known files'.

results.attack: Holder of the dedup secret + the ID index recovers a 6-digit field of a templated document
results.detail: 482914 HMACs over a 1001-byte document in 2.83 s (one core, CPython hashlib; x86_64). Tahoe-LAFS 'learn-the-remaining-information' attack.

results.attack: Secret sealed to the device X25519 key and signed by the homelab; cloud tries to read and to swap it
results.expected: cloud cannot read; swap detected; device reads
results.observed: cloud cannot read; swap detected; device reads
results.detail: Needs the device key to reach the homelab authentically first (A5), or the cloud swaps the device key instead.

results.attack: Cloud forges a receipt with its own key
results.detail: Ed25519 over 'reliquary-commit-v1\n' || JSON; binding fields device_id, dedup_id, size, meta_sha256.

results.detail: Ed25519 over 'reliquary-commit-v1\n' || JSON; binding fields device_id, dedup_id, size, meta_sha256.

results.attack: Worker substitutes H1's restore key; homelab re-encrypts the restore to it
results.detail: ADR-0001 §6 re-encrypts to 'the requesting device's own public key'; if the homelab learns that key from the Worker, a restore is disclosed.

results.attack: Same substitution; homelab admits device keys only with a signature by a key the cloud lacks
results.detail: Tailnet-Lock analogue. Who holds the admitting key (admin, homelab, or an existing device) is D3/OD-05.

results.attack: Cloud holds the stored hash of a 50-bit invite code (fast hash); offline search cost
results.detail: measured 1,024,717 SHA-256/s on one core in CPython; 2^50 at that rate = 35 core-years. This is a single-core CPython floor, not a GPU figure: GPU rates are orders of magnitude higher and were not measured. Relevant only if a homelab-verified secret is derived from the invite code (D3).
